newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends mostly up on LME gains.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends mostly up on LME gains.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended mostly up on Thursday on overnight gains on the London Metal Exchange but profit-taking pushed prices down from their highs, traders said.
The most active March 1997 contract ended at 20,160 yuan ($2,428) per tonne, rising 90 yuan. It opened at 20,330 yuan, hitting an intra-day high of 20,350 and a low of 20,110.
December fell 80 to 20,150, January rose 10 to 20,110, February 40 to 20,120, April 60 to 20,150, May 30 to 20,180 and June 200 to 20,300.
Combined volume rose to 76,790 tonnes from 64,680.
Copper opened higher on overnight LME gains but profit-taking pushed prices steadily down for most of the session, with investors cautious.
"Many investors wanted to liquidate their positions and stay on the sidelines until the market direction becomes clear," one trader said.
"The firm spot copper price supported futures despite poor long-term fundamentals," he added. The price of spot copper is around 20,500 yuan per tonne in Shanghai.
Traders said investors did not dare to build large positions with the short-term LME trend unclear.

"It is time for investors to adjust their positions," a second trader said. "Long position holders liquidated their positions at high levels while short position holders liquidated theirs at low levels."
Analysts said the LME continued to be the main factor influencing Shanghai copper due to a lack of domestic market-moving news.
Aluminium ended little changed. December fell 10 to 13,690 yuan per tonne, January did not trade and February was unchanged at 14,000. Combined volume rose to 500 tonnes from 400.
